questions.question: 8 pens and 14 pencils cost as much as 12 pens and 5 pencils. The ratio of the cost of one pen to the cost of one pencil is:
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

Cost of 8 pens and 14 pencils = Cost of 12 pens and 5 pencils

**Calculation:-**

Let Cost of 1 pen be x and Cost of 1 pencil be y,

According to question-

⇒ 8x + 14y = 12x + 5y

⇒ 4x = 9y

⇒ x/y = 9/4

∴ **Ratio of cost of one pen to the cost of one pencil is 9 : 4.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 96 cm² and its volume is 672 cm³. Its diameter is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of the cylinder = 96 cm²

The volume of the cylinder = 672 cm³

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh

Diameter = 2 × radius

**Calculation:**

Here, πr²h = 672 -----(1)

And 2πrh = 96 -----(2)

Dividing (1) by (2) we get,

⇒ r/2 = 7

⇒ r = 14

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 14 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

questions.question: The time taken by a boat to go 34 km upstream is 25% more than the time it takes to go 40 km downstream. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 125% : 100% = 5 : 4

Time = Distance ÷ Speed ⇒ [34 ÷ (u − 4)] ÷ [40 ÷ (u + 4)] = 5 ÷ 4

⇒ (u + 4) ÷ (u − 4) = (5 × 40) ÷ (4 × 34) = 200 ÷ 136 = 25 ÷ 17

Applying Componendo & Dividendo: u ÷ 4 = (25 + 17) ÷ (25 − 17) = 42 ÷ 8

⇒ u = 42 × 4 ÷ 8 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the stream (v) = 4 km/h

Distance upstream (Dᵤ) = 34 km

Distance downstream (Dd) = 40 km

Time taken upstream (Tᵤ) is 25% more than Time taken downstream (Td)

**Formula Used:**

Speed Upstream = u − v

Speed Downstream = u + v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
 
 Downstream (With Stream)
 Distance = 40 km | Speed = u + 4 | Time = t
 
 
 Upstream (Against Stream)
 Distance = 34 km | Speed = u − 4 | Time = 1.25t
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the speed of the boat in still water be u km/h.

⇒ Td = 40 ÷ (u + 4)

⇒ Tᵤ = 34 ÷ (u − 4)

⇒ Tᵤ = Td + 25% of Td = 1.25 × Td = (5 ÷ 4) × Td

⇒ 34 ÷ (u − 4) = [40 ÷ (u + 4)] × (5 ÷ 4)

⇒ 34 ÷ (u − 4) = 50 ÷ (u + 4)

⇒ 34(u + 4) = 50(u − 4)

⇒ 34u + 136 = 50u − 200

⇒ 50u − 34u = 136 + 200

⇒ 16u = 336

⇒ u = 336 ÷ 16 = 21 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 21 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, the speed of the boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

Using the same downstream and upstream speeds, the speed of the current/stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept in Rivers

When a boat moves downstream, the relative speed is the sum of the boat's speed and the stream's speed. Upstream, it is their difference as the stream opposes the motion.

questions.question: The average weight of 20 students in a group is 54 kg. If 12 students of average weight 52 kg join the group and 7 students of average weight 56 kg leave the group, then what will be the average weight (in kg) of the remaining students in the group?
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

Average weight of 20 students = 54 kg

Average weight of 12 students = 52 kg

Average weight of 7 students = 56 kg

**Formula used:-**

Average = (Sum of all weight)/(Total no. of weight)

**Calculation:-**

According to question-

⇒ (Sum of 20 students)/20 = 54

⇒ Sum of 20 students = 54 × 20

⇒ Sum of 20 students = 1080

∴ Sum of 12 students = 52 × 12

⇒ Sum of 12 students = 624

⇒ Sum of 7 students = 56 × 7

⇒ Sum of 7 students = 392

Average of remaining students = (Sum of 20 students + Sum of 12 students - Sum of 7 students)/(20 + 12 - 7)

Average of remaining students = (1080 + 624 - 392)/25

Average of remaining students = 1312/25 = 52.48

∴ **Average of remaining students is 52.48. **

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers successive discounts of 10% and k%. Customers get items marked at Rs. 1,200 for Rs. 864. What is the value of k?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

First discount of 10% reduces the Marked Price from ₹1200 to ₹1080.

The final Selling Price after the second discount is ₹864.

Second discount amount = 1080 − 864 = ₹216.

Value of k = (216 ÷ 1080) × 100 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1200

Selling Price (SP) = ₹864

Discounts = 10% and k%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed8518b9cc678de0dec4de7a12b168769d1f03615df8508e241752bc8141259d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 10% discount = 1200 × (90 / 100)

⇒ Mid Price = ₹1080

⇒ Discount amount given for k% = 1080 − 864

⇒ Discount amount = ₹216

⇒ k = (Discount / Mid Price) × 100

⇒ k = (216 / 1080) × 100

⇒ k = 1 / 5 × 100 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are applied successively, the effective equivalent discount is given by the formula: (a + b − ab / 100)%.

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. SP is calculated as: SP = MP − Discount.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

A shopkeeper may mark up the price above the Cost Price (CP) and then offer a discount. Total Profit is still evaluated based on the final SP − CP.

questions.question: Three persons start a morning walk together. Their steps measure 70 cm, 75 cm and 80 cm, respectively. What is the minimum distance each should walk, so that all of them can cover the same distance in complete steps?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three persons start a morning walk together and their step measure 70cm, 75cm, and 80cm respectively.

**Calculation:**

Their steps measure 70cm, 75cm, and 80cm respectively

Minimum distance covered by each = LCM(70, 75, 80)

For LCM

⇒ 70 = 2 × 5 × 7

⇒ 75 = 3 × 5²

⇒ 80 = 2⁴ × 5

Now, LCM = 2⁴ × 5² × 3 × 7 = 8400

**So, the minimum distance covered by each is 8400cm.**

questions.question: ​A sum amounts to Rs. 4,260 in 5 years at the rate of 4% p.a. simple interest. What will be the simple interest (in Rs. nearest to a Rs.) on the same sum for 4(1)/(5) years at the rate of 8(1)/(2)% p.a.?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum amounts to Rs. 4,260 in 5 years at the rate of 4% p.a. simple interest.

The same sum for 4(1)/(5) years at the rate of 8(1)/(2)% p.a.

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + S.I

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time and S.I = Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Let the principal be x.

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ (x × 4 × 5)/100

⇒ 20 x/100 = x/5

Amount = P + S.I

⇒ 4260 = x + x/5

⇒ 6 x/5 = 4260

⇒ x = 3550

Simple interest on the same sum for 4(1)/(5) years at the rate of 8(1)/(2)% p.a. is,

S.I = (3550 × 8(1)/(2) × 4(1)/(5) )/100

⇒ (3550 × 17/2 × 21/5)/100

⇒ 1267.35 ≈ 1267.

**∴ The Required Simple Interest is Rs. 1267. **

questions.question: Bike A moving at a speed of 30 km/h covers some distance for 2 hours, while another bike B moving at a speed of 35 km/h covers the same distance as bike A. What is the ratio of the time taken by bike A to that taken by bike B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Bike A moves at a speed of 30 km/h.

Bike A covers some distance for 2 hours.

Bike B moves at a speed of 35 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ 30 × 2 = 60 km

Time is taken by bike B to cover the distance.

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ 60over35 = 12over7 hours

The ratio of the time taken by bike A to that taken by bike B.

⇒ 2 : 12over7 (Multiply by 7 on both sides)

⇒ 14 : 12

⇒ 7 : 6

**∴ The ratio of the time taken by bike A to that taken by bike B is 7 : 6.**

questions.question:
​ x is the smallest number of 5-digits which when divided by 10, 15, 24, 35 and 42, leaves a remainder 7 in each case.

The sum of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of the divisors (10, 15, 24, 35, 42) = 840.

The smallest 5-digit number is 10000.

Smallest 5-digit multiple of 840 = 10000 + (840 − 760) = 10080.

Since the remainder is 7 in each case, the required number x = 10080 + 7 = 10087.

Sum of the digits = 1 + 0 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The divisors are 10, 15, 24, 35, and 42.

The remainder in each case is 7.

The number x is the smallest 5-digit number satisfying this condition.

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = (Multiple of LCM of given divisors) + Remainder

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, find the prime factorization of each divisor:

⇒ 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ 35 = 5 × 7

⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ LCM(10, 15, 24, 35, 42) = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840

⇒ The smallest 5-digit number is 10000.

⇒ Now, divide 10000 by 840 to find the nearest multiple:

⇒ 10000 ÷ 840 gives a quotient of 11 and a remainder of 760.

⇒ The smallest 5-digit multiple of 840 = 10000 + (840 − 760) = 10080.

⇒ To get a remainder of 7 when divided by the given numbers, add 7 to this multiple.

⇒ x = 10080 + 7 = 10087

⇒ Sum of the digits of x = 1 + 0 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r in each case, the required number is of the general form: k × LCM(a, b, c) + r (where k is a positive integer).

LCM and Remainder Concept (Different Remainders)

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders p, q, and s respectively, such that the difference between the divisor and remainder is constant i.e., (a − p) = (b − q) = (c − s) = d, the required number is of the form: k × LCM(a, b, c) − d.

Highest Common Factor (HCF) Rules

To find the greatest number that will divide x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, find the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).
</p

questions.question: A group of persons can complete a piece of work in a certain time. If there were 4 more persons, they would take 2 days less to complete it. If there were 6 persons less, they would take 4 days more to complete it. What is the number of persons, initially, in the group?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If 4 Persons more then take 2 days less.

And 6 Persons less, take 4 days more.

**Solution:**

Let person be n and days be x

Total work = n × x

According to Question,

⇒ n × x = (n + 4) (x - 2) --------------(1)

⇒ n × x = (n - 6) (x + 4) --------------(2)

Solving Equation (1) and (2) we get,

⇒ 2n - 4x = -8

⇒ 4x - 2n = 8 -----------------(3)

⇒ -4n + 6x = -24

⇒ 2n - 3x = 12 ----------------(4)

Adding Equation (3) and (4) We get,
